title: Introduce yourself
script:
Say this five times, then record yourself on your phone and listen back. Speak slowly and clearly.  
  
**“Hi, this is Jawad, dispatcher with Blue Line Transport, MC number 1-2-3-4-5-6. I’m calling about your load from Joliet, Illinois to Charlotte, North Carolina. Is it still available?”**  
  
Then change the city pair to: Dallas, TX → Atlanta, GA and Lebanon, OH → Owensboro, KY. (Blue Line Transport is a practice carrier used throughout this course.)

title: The phonetic alphabet
script: On calls you will spell MC numbers, emails and load numbers. Learn this table and practise spelling your name, your email, and **“Ship Express, load 12354.”**

title: The load read-back
script: After a broker gives you details, read them back: **“So that’s pickup Monday, 7 to 8 AM Eastern, Green Bay Packaging in Lebanon, Ohio; delivery Monday noon Central, Tracco in Owensboro, Kentucky; 10 skids, 2,000 pounds, box truck. Correct?”**

title: The equipment questions
script:
Practise this with a broker who has just said “It’s a dry van load, Joliet to Atlanta.”  
  
**“Great. What’s the commodity and the total weight? How many pallets — are they stackable? Is it dock to dock, live load and live unload? Any length restriction, load bars or air-ride needed?”**  
  
Then do the same for a reefer (“What’s the setpoint — continuous or cycle? Pre-cool required?”) and a flatbed (“Dimensions? Tarps — what size drop? Chains or straps?”).

title: The lane briefing
script:
You found a load and the carrier approved it. Brief the driver in 20 seconds:  
  
**“Carlos, your next load is Dallas, Texas to Atlanta, Georgia, about 780 miles, mostly I-20 east. Pickup is tomorrow at 8 AM Central; delivery Thursday at 7 AM Eastern — remember Atlanta is an hour ahead. I’ll send the full details on WhatsApp.”**  
  
Then do the same for Joliet → Charlotte and Laredo → Chicago.

title: Refusing an unsafe request politely
script:
Broker: “Can’t your guy just push through tonight?”  
  
**“I understand the timing is tight. He’s out of hours at 8 PM Central and needs his 10-hour break, so the realistic delivery is 10 AM tomorrow. I can send you a tracking update when he’s rolling. Would 10 AM work for the receiver?”**  
  
Calm, factual, and offering a solution. Practise until it sounds natural.

title: Verifying a COI with the agent
script:
Call the phone number on the COI (or the insurer’s official number):  
  
**“Hi, this is Jawad, dispatcher for Blue Line Transport, MC 1298456. I’m confirming a certificate of insurance dated September 15, 2026. Can you confirm the auto liability and cargo policies are active, the limits are $1 million and $100,000, and that the 2022 Freightliner, VIN ending 4471, is on the schedule? Also, are there any cargo exclusions for reefer breakdown?”**  
  
Write down the name of the person, the date and the answers.

title: The first 15 seconds
script:
**“Hi, this is Jawad with Blue Line Transport, MC 1298456. I’m calling about your load LL-448210, Chicago to Charlotte, picking up Wednesday. Is it still available?”**  
  
If yes: **“Great. What’s the commodity and weight, and what are the pickup and delivery appointments?”** Rate comes after the facts (Module 8).

title: Pitching a plan
script: **“Mike, I have Bolingbrook to Atlanta, 715 miles, 12 empty, picks up Wednesday at 9, delivers Thursday at 1. The broker offered $1,600. I got them to $1,750, which is $2.41 a mile, under our $2.59 break-even by itself. But Atlanta is strong: I have a Thursday reload to Columbus for $1,700, so the two loads average $2.62, and Carlos is back near home Friday with hours left. Do you want me to book both?”**

title: The negotiation
script: You: “Hi, this is Jawad with Blue Line Transport, MC 1298456, calling about your Bolingbrook to Atlanta load for Wednesday. Is it still available?” — Broker: “Yes.” — You: “Great. What’s the commodity and weight, and what are the pickup and delivery appointments?” — Broker: “Paper products, 38,500 pounds. Pickup Wednesday 9 to 11, delivery Thursday 1 PM.” — You: “Okay. What are you paying on it?” — Broker: “$1,600.” — You: “For 727 miles with a same-day pickup I need $2,000. This lane has been running around $2.60 a mile.” (Then stop talking.) — Broker: “I can go $1,700.” — You: “Meet me at $1,800 and I’ll book it now.” — Broker: “$1,750 is the best I can do.” — You: “Let me confirm with my carrier. I’ll call you back in five minutes.”

title: The loaded update call
script: **“Hi, this is Jawad with Blue Line Transport, MC 1298456, updating load PF-20931. We’re loaded as of 10:35 Central: 22 pallets, 38,500 pounds, seal number 4-4-7-1-0-2-3. Tracking is active. ETA Thursday noon Eastern for the 1 PM appointment. I’ll send the BOL now.”**

title: The late ETA call
script: “Hi, this is Jawad with Blue Line, load PF-20931. Our driver was held by a highway closure on I-24 and will not make the 1 PM appointment. Realistic ETA is 2:50 PM Eastern. Can you ask the receiver for a later slot today? I’ll send the update in writing now.” Structure: load · what happened · honest ETA · request · written follow-up. Always before the appointment time.
